newsitem.title: USA: Boise Cascade strike idles 2,000 workers.
newsitem.headline: Boise Cascade strike idles 2,000 workers.

text.p: More than 2,000 unionized Boise Cascade Corp workers at nine lumber mills have been idled by a strike and no new negotiations are scheduled, a company official said on Friday.
About 800 workers represented by the Southern Council of Industrial Workers struck three wood-products plants in Louisiana on September 12 in a dispute over health insurance and other benefits.
The strike's effect spread to the Pacific Northwest this week, when striking Louisiana workers asked for and received support from unionized workers at six plants in Washington and Oregon.
Doug Bartels, a spokesman for the company, said 200 hourly workers have crossed picket lines to work at the three Louisiana plants, leaving 600 off the job.
Another 1,600 workers in Washington and Oregon have walked off the job to honor picket lines established by strikers who traveled to the region from Louisiana.
The sympathy walkout by members of the Western Council of Industrial Workers reportedly is permitted by the union's contracts with Boise Cascade. Union officials could not be reached for comment.
Bartels said it was too soon to assess the impact of the strike, although he said some of the nine affected mills are being operated by supervisors "on at least a partial basis."

Ragen MacKenzie analyst Paul Latta said the company probably could work from inventories for several days more, but he estimated that by October 3 the strike would begin costing the company $0.01 a share in net earnings each day.

Without the strike, he estimated the company post a loss of $0.10 a share in the fourth quarter and a loss of $0.64 a share for the year. For all of 1995, the company had net earnings of $5.14 a share.
"It's not the best timing in the world because lumber prices are near a two-year high," he said.
Bartels said a federal mediator has been called in to help resolve the conflict with the Louisiana workers.
"We very much want to get this resolved, and get back to the negotiating table," he said. "We expect to have a next meeting soon."
